Britannia, Nestle, ITC: FMCG stocks decline as SC orders separate warning labels for high sugar, salt, fat
sum: Rejecting a proposal for a single combined warning symbol, the court said each nutrient must have a separate hexagonal label carrying the words "High Fat", "High Sugar" or "High Salt", along with a corresponding pictogram.
Food companies will subsequently be given a 365-day transition period to comply with the new labelling requirements. Image: Shutterstock

Shares of FMCG companies such as Britannia Industries, Nestle India, ITC and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) are likely to remain in focus on Friday, November 27, after the Supreme Court on Thursday directed that packaged foods high in sugar, salt or fat must carry separate and prominent warning labels for each of these nutrients.

The Supreme Court said a single combined hexagon would "undermine the very objective" of the warning-label exercise. It directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to implement the rules within the four-month timeline proposed by the food regulator.

In its 131-page judgment, a bench comprising Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed FSSAI to address design and threshold-related shortcomings in its draft warning-label framework. The court also asked the regulator to adhere to its proposed implementation timeline.
The ruling will impact everything from chips and biscuits to fizzy drinks.

"A consumer in India is entitled to no less protection, and no less information, than a consumer in the United States or the United Kingdom," the court said, calling reports of differing practices by global companies "deeply troubling" if true. It named no company and urged multinationals to adopt uniform standards across countries.

The company has invested in the tobacco sector because it achieves high profit margins and is less seasonal than other business models.

Another important business area for ITC is the hotel and hospitality management sector. The company is the largest hotel operator in India and operates the renowned ITC Hotels chain, which is considered a leader in the Asian luxury segment. The hotels offer top-class accommodations and culinary experiences, contributing significantly to ITC's positioning as a leading company in the hospitality industry.

How Did JK Shah List Itself on the NSE Without an IPO? Understanding Demerger Listings and How They Work
sum: J.K. Shah Commerce Education Limited (JKSCEL), known for its CA and commerce coaching business, made its stock market debut on November 18, 2026, on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). However, unlike most newly listed companies, it did not launch an Initial Public Offering (IPO), invite public subscriptions or raise fresh capital through a public issue. Instead, the company entered the stock market through a demerger from Veranda Learning Solutions Limited.

The development highlights an alternative route through which businesses can become independently listed in India. Several companies, including Jio Financial Services, Piramal Pharma and ITC Hotels, have previously followed similar routes. Understanding how this process works can help investors distinguish between an IPO and a demerger listing.

JKSCEL's stock market debut followed a composite scheme of arrangement involving Veranda Learning Solutions. Under the scheme, Veranda separated its commerce education business and transferred it to JKSCEL, an existing wholly owned subsidiary of Veranda.

The resulting company brought together several established education brands, including J.K. Shah Classes, BB Virtuals, Navkar Digital Institute, Tapasya College of Commerce and Logic School of Management. The objective was to create a dedicated commerce education company with independent leadership, operational flexibility and a sharper growth strategy.

The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Chennai Bench, approved the composite scheme on August 20, 2026. Following the completion of the required formalities, JKSCEL was admitted for trading on the NSE and BSE from November 18, 2026.
Its shares debuted at Rs.218 on the NSE and Rs.219 on the BSE, giving the company a market capitalisation of approximately Rs.2,104 crore.

A demerger involves separating one or more business undertakings from an existing company and transferring them into another entity. The resulting company can operate independently, with its own management, financial statements, shareholders and stock market valuation.

He further said that companies will be able to sustain their growth momentum in the second half of FY27 (H2 FY27) if travel demand recovers. sum: Shares of diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd rallied nearly 4 percent on Monday, November 16, to hit an over-five-month high of Rs 296, after reports said consumer spending on its acquired personal care and hygiene brands, Savlon and Nimyle, is expected to more than double to cross Rs 2,000 crore in the medium term, driven by product innovation, portfolio expansion and deeper market penetration.

The rally lifted broader fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) stocks, propelling the Nifty FMCG index up nearly 2 percent to touch a near three-month high of 47,708.10. With this, the index emerged as the top sectoral gainer in today’s trading session.

While peers like Tata Consumer Products gained over 3.5 percent and Nestle India 2.5 percent and Godrej Consumer Products rose 2.6 percent at close, Patanjali, United Breweries and Colgate Palmolive (India) bucked the trend, slipping 4.8 percent, 1.8 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.
Shares of ITC opened at Rs 285 and rose 3.91 percent to touch an over-five-month high of Rs 296.15. The stock settled 3.54 percent higher at Rs 295.10, on the NSE.

The immediate trigger for ITC shares was the growth outlook for its acquired Savlon and Nimyle brands. Post their acquisitions, both brands have registered a multi-fold growth under ITC's ownership and together have crossed Rs 1,000 crore in consumer spends, growing at over 20 percent annually, according to industry experts.

The conglomerate had acquired Savlon from Johnson & Johnson in February 2015 and has scaled up the brand nearly nine-fold over the past decade while Nimyle from Kolkata-based Arpita Agro Products in June 2018, has grown eight-fold in around seven to eight years since its acquisition.
“We expect the runway ahead to be just as exciting as the distance we’ve covered,” Sameer Satpathy, divisional chief executive of the personal care products business, told the news agency PTI.

ITC stock plans to absorb Yoga Bar maker after board approval
sum: ITC's board approved a scheme on November 2, 2026, to merge wholly owned Sproutlife Foods Private Limited into the parent company. ET Retail reported that the scheme is subject to statutory and regulatory approvals and is intended to take effect from April 1, 2026.

Sproutlife makes bars, muesli, oats, protein-rich foods and peanut butter under the digital-first Yoga Bar brand. It reported turnover of INR 451.71 crore, total assets of INR 150.07 crore and net worth of INR 5.22 crore in fiscal 2026, based on audited standalone accounts.

ITC said the merger should integrate operations, improve the use of financial and managerial resources and simplify the group structure by reducing the number of operating entities. Because Sproutlife is wholly owned, its shares held by ITC and its nominees will be cancelled when the scheme becomes effective. ITC will issue no new shares, and the shareholding pattern will not change.

The transaction comes after ITC's September-quarter results. ET Retail reported an 18.5 percent decline in consolidated net profit to INR 4,229 crore, while net revenue rose 5 percent to INR 20,454 crore. Weaker cigarette earnings weighed on profitability, although the FMCG, agriculture and paper businesses delivered stronger growth.

For investors, the merger is primarily a structural step rather than an immediate share issuance or ownership event. The key next milestones are the required approvals and the execution of the scheme, alongside progress in ITC's non-cigarette businesses.
Investors can place ITC's corporate developments alongside the BSE Sensex market environment.

The rally comes despite the cigarette-to-FMCG conglomerate reporting a weak set of Q2 FY27 results, with consolidated profit declining nearly 19% year-on-year and EBITDA margins contracting sharply.

On Wednesday, ITC shares surged as much as 3.7% to an intraday high of ₹283.50 on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to around ₹3.51 lakh crore. The stock has gained around 6% since the company announced its Q2 FY27 results after market hours on Monday.

As many as 36.66 crore ITC shares, representing approximately 2.9 per cent of the company’s outstanding equity, were traded in the block deal window at an average price of ₹257 per share. The identities of the buyers and sellers were not immediately disclosed.

The transaction follows a disclosure earlier this week that US-based fund house GQG Partners LLC had sold 3.97 crore ITC shares through on-market transactions between May 28, 2025, and October 5, 2026. sum: As per a stock exchange filing, ITC Infotech will first acquire a 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds from founder and promoter Ashok Soota for Rs 1,330 crore, with the purchase split across two tranches. The initial transaction will then be followed by a share swap between the two companies, under which shareholders will receive 25 ITC Infotech shares for every 81 Happiest Minds shares held.

Following the completion of the merger, ITC Infotech will be listed on the stock exchanges through a backdoor listing. ITC Ltd will hold a 73.4% stake in the merged entity, while Soota and his promoter entities will own 7.6%. Public shareholders will hold the remaining 19%.

Happiest Minds has been assigned an equity value of Rs 6,167 crore for the transaction, while ITC Infotech has been valued at Rs 11,920 crore. Together, the two companies have a combined valuation of more than Rs 18,000 crore.

Ashok Soota, who founded Happiest Minds in 2011, said he was delighted that, after the completion of the legal formalities, the company would become an important part of a larger organisation through its amalgamation with ITC Infotech. He said the two organisations were aligned in their values and shared vision for the future, while their business portfolios had significant complementarity that would ensure synergies.
The company said the transaction would make the merged entity India's 11th-largest IT services company, with aggregate annual revenue of Rs 7,033 crore in fiscal 2026.

sum: ITC Infotech is reportedly moving closer to acquiring a controlling stake of around 44% in Bengaluru-based Happiest Minds Technologies from founder Ashok Soota and promoter entities, in what could become one of the bigger consolidation moves in India's mid-tier IT services market.
Multiple media reports have placed the potential transaction value at around ₹2,800 crore to ₹2,900 crore. Neither ITC Infotech nor Happiest Minds has formally announced a transaction so far.

Earlier reports had suggested a possible two-part structure, with ITC Infotech directly acquiring around 22% of Happiest Minds from the promoters and the remaining promoter holding potentially being part of a separate share-based transaction. A price range of around ₹390–₹400 per share was reported for the direct purchase component.
The final transaction structure, pricing and timelines have not been officially disclosed.
Founded by IT industry veteran Ashok Soota in 2011, Happiest Minds has built its business around digital engineering and newer enterprise technologies.

The company today describes itself as an AI-first digital engineering player, with capabilities spanning product and digital engineering, GenAI, cybersecurity, analytics, cloud and infrastructure management, automation and the Internet of Things.

That portfolio makes the reported transaction strategically relevant for ITC Infotech as enterprise technology spending shifts increasingly toward AI-led transformation, cloud modernization, data platforms and engineering services.

sum: ITC might need to hike prices by “at least 15%” to pass on the overall impact to consumers, if not higher. ITC gets over 40% of its revenue from cigarettes.
Shares of India's largest cigarette maker ITC Ltd. fell the most in six years after the government imposed higher tax on tobacco products.

From 1 February 2026, cigarettes will be charged an excise duty of ₹2,050-8,500 per 1,000 sticks, according to a government notification released late Wednesday. That's on top of GST at 40% on tobacco-based products and cigarettes—also kicking in from 1 February.

ITC's share price dropped as much as 9.8%, the most since 2020, while Godfrey Phillips India Ltd. dropped 17.6% on the BSE. ITC sells cigarette brands like Classic and Gold Flake, while Godfrey sells Marlboro and Four Square.

On 22 September 2025, the Narendra Modi government cut GST rates on soaps to small cars in the biggest indirect tax reforms since goods and services tax first came into effect on 1 July 2017. The rationalisation reduced the number of GST slabs to two (5% and 18%) from four (5%, 12%, 18% and 28%). A new GST slab of 40% was introduced for so-called sin goods—tobacco products and luxury items such as SUVs to Swiss watches and handbags.

The GST compensation cess was scrapped as part of the overhaul, which would have reduced the effective tax rate on tobacco products, but now an even higher excise duty has replaced it. The taxation is expected to make up the shortfall in GST revenue from other product categories.
At 25.3 crore people, India has the second-highest population of tobacco users.
